name: El
role: High god and patriarch of the Canaanite pantheon
fun_fact: El is called 'Bull El' in Ugaritic poetry, and his consent is still needed when Baal wins kingship.

name: Asherah
role: Mother goddess and consort of El
fun_fact: Her Ugaritic name is Athirat, and her epithet 'Lady of the Sea' may describe a goddess of the sea; in the Hebrew Bible, asherah can also mean a wooden cult object.

name: Baal
role: Storm god and king of the gods
fun_fact: Baal's palace stands on Mount Sapan, a mountain north of Ugarit that is still called Jebel al-Aqra.

name: Anat
role: Warrior goddess and sister of Baal
fun_fact: In one battle scene Anat wades in blood up to her knees, and the poem treats her violence as both terrifying and necessary.

name: Yam
role: Sea god and rival of Baal
fun_fact: Yam is also called Judge River, and his defeat by Baal is echoed in biblical poetry about the sea.

name: Mot
role: God of death and the underworld
fun_fact: Mot is called 'the beloved of El', which makes his struggle with Baal a family quarrel as well as a cosmic one.

name: Kothar-wa-Khasis
fun_fact: His name means 'Skillful and Wise', and he makes both the clubs that defeat Yam and the palace that confirms Baal's rule.

name: Danel
role: Righteous judge and father of Aqhat
fun_fact: Danel is named in the book of Ezekiel as a model of righteousness, which suggests that his story was still known in Israel.

name: Aqhat
role: Son of Danel and owner of the bow
fun_fact: Aqhat's refusal to give up his bow is often read as youthful pride, but the broken text leaves his motives uncertain.

name: Kirta
role: King and hero of the Kirta epic
fun_fact: Kirta is one of the few human heroes in Ugaritic myth, and his epic breaks off before the succession is resolved.
